clue.text: Cast in 10 officers

indicators.note: read as 'C as T in', telling the solver to put a C where the T stands in the other answer

parts.note: the answer to 10 across, which means courteous

explanation.surface: Somebody casts a set of officers in a play called 10.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' is not an abbreviation: split it as 'C as T', so the C takes the place of the T in POLITE (10 across).
explanation.definitionFit: A plural collective noun: officers of the law make up the force collectively known by this name.

clue.text: Sign of fish found swimming upstream

indicators.note: in a down clue, swimming upstream means the letters run from bottom to top, so they are read backwards

parts.note: Finding Nemo is the film about a lost clownfish, so the fish that is found is Nemo

explanation.surface: A fish swimming against the current is taken as a portent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' is part of the reference: the fish in the film Finding Nemo.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a portent or augury is a sign of something to come.

clue.text: Rotten cheese? It's found in Greenland

definitions.text: Rotten cheese? It's found in Greenland

indicators.note: something rotten has gone bad and broken down, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about mouldy cheese turning up in Greenland.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of CHEESE and ITS are mixed up, and the whole clue also describes the answer: the great frozen expanses that cover Greenland.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenland is mostly covered by a vast continental glacier, the planet's second largest frozen mass.

clue.text: Cover provided, if born and raised within Eurozone borders

indicators.note: within says one set of letters is placed inside the other
the borders of a word are its first and last letters
in a down clue, raised means the word is lifted to read from the bottom up, backwards

explanation.surface: An insurance-style condition: cover applies if you were born and brought up in the euro area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' looks like 'brought up' alongside 'born', but in a down clue it lifts the word to read upwards; 'provided, if' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to dress someone in a robe is to cover or clothe them.

clue.text: Felon with power abused imperial crown

indicators.note: abused means mistreated or knocked about, so the letters are rearranged; the answer plus the word power make up the fodder

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer with authority has mistreated the emperor's crown.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer's letters together with POWER can be rearranged into IMPERIAL CROWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a felon is a lawbreaker, someone convicted of a serious offence.

clue.text: Olympic season at variance with feeling

indicators.note: being at variance means differing or out of line, so the letters are set out in a different order

explanation.surface: The Olympic season is somehow out of step with public feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' does double duty in the surface reading of 'at variance', but in the parse it belongs to the anagram fodder with OLYMPIC SEASON.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with feeling, with sympathy and warmth, is doing it in a caring, tender-hearted way.

clue.text: Devil played a role and got stuck

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
an actor who played a role acted

explanation.surface: An actor playing the devil dried up on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wedged firmly in place, like a wisdom tooth or blocked bowel, is said to be jammed in this way.

clue.text: Stepford wife takes her top off and reveals bum

indicators.note: taking off her top removes the first letter of the woman's name

parts.note: Bette Midler starred in the 2004 film The Stepford Wives

explanation.surface: A suburban housewife strips off and shows her backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' looks like a backside, but it is the American sense: a loafer.
explanation.definitionFit: In the American sense, a bum is a layabout or loafer who avoids work.

clue.text: With regard to finance, capital loss is staggering

indicators.note: the loss of the capital, the first letter, is a deletion

explanation.surface: A financial report says a loss of capital is shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital loss' reads as an accounting term, but it means dropping the F from FUNDING.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something staggering is amazing, so surprising it leaves you reeling.

clue.text: The mind of a sincere Brummie

indicators.note: the answer is part of the letters of the following words, so it is taken out of them

explanation.surface: An honest person from Birmingham has a fine mind.
explanation.walkthrough: A Brummie is someone from Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose sense: the large front part of the brain, seat of thought, stands for the intellect.

clue.text: Courteous and quiet Eliot composition can make poet almost ill and another inflamed within

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A quiet poem by T S Eliot is mannerly enough to sicken and inflame other poets.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple-wordplay clue. Also: POET with IL (almost 'ill') mixed up, signalled by 'make'; and POE (poet almost) with LIT (another word for inflamed) inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being courteous means having good manners and treating others with respect.

clue.text: Come to judge brute briefly infiltrating our chaps in action

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so one set of letters goes into the other
in action means busy and moving about, so these letters are rearranged
briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A brutish man comes before a judge after sneaking among our men in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come to judge' is a fair gloss: the Latin writ orders a detained person to be brought before a court.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin legal writ, 'you shall have the body', ordering a detained person to be brought before a court.

clue.text: Opposition to most angina treatment

indicators.note: treatment means processing or handling, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Most angina treatment meets resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: hostility or active opposition between rivals.

clue.text: Articulation that is ultimately quick on the uptake and keen to change

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the final letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A clever, eager person is quick to understand how things are put together.
explanation.walkthrough: Double wordplay: also an anagram of KEEN, signalled by 'to change'.
explanation.definitionFit: An articulation is anatomically a joint, the leg's hinged joint being one example.

clue.text: Section of the nursery where tennis players sleep?

definitions.meaning: plant nurseries have patches of fine soil for germinating plants from sown grains
seeded tennis players, the ranked ones, might whimsically sleep in beds for seeds

explanation.surface: Part of a nursery where tennis stars take a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant nursery's beds where sown grains sprout; whimsically, beds for seeded players.

clue.text: Dined with artist, bill's covered for both parties

indicators.note: 'bill's covered' reads as 'bill has covered', so the other letters go inside the bill

parts.note: a bill is the bill, here meaning has covered
to have dined is to have eaten: ate
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: After a meal with an artist, the bill is paid for both diners.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'bill's covered' as 'bill has covered': the bill wraps around the other pieces. RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A bilateral agreement or deal involves two sides, binding both of them.

clue.text: Starting over, the ophthalmic surgeons manage to get the wrong instrument!

indicators.note: starting picks the letter each word starts with

explanation.surface: Eye surgeons start again and manage to pick up the wrong tool.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is in 'the wrong instrument': this one is for examining ears, not eyes, so it is wrong for ophthalmic surgeons.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical tool used to look into the ear canal and eardrum.

clue.text: Culottes Lafayette pulled up somewhat too tight, hence his voice

indicators.note: pulled up means drawn back, so the letters are read from right to left
somewhat means part of, so the letters are taken from inside the words

explanation.surface: Lafayette's culottes are hitched up a bit too snug, so his voice goes squeaky.
explanation.walkthrough: Culottes were the knee-breeches of French aristocrats such as Lafayette.
explanation.definitionFit: A high, squeaky male voice above the normal range, comically blamed on tight breeches.

clue.text: Tall island pine

definitions.meaning: a tall person is lanky, of great length
... Island is the island off New York

explanation.surface: A tall pine tree on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: lengthy in stature, part of an island's name near New York, and yearning.

clue.text: Martyr men

parts.note: two men's names, Vic and Tim
two men's names, Vic and Tim

explanation.surface: Martyr men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'men' supplies two names, Vic and Tim, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A martyr is someone who suffers or dies for a cause, a sufferer or sacrifice.

clue.text: Miss aromatic stew in food supplies

indicators.note: a stew is a mixture cooked together, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A stew that is missing its aromatic touch among the rations.
explanation.definitionFit: An army's department providing food, and by extension the supplies of provisions themselves.

clue.text: A place to stay in a remote location

indicators.note: in says the answer is found within the letters of the next words

explanation.surface: Lodging at an out-of-the-way spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside hotel for motorists is somewhere to stay the night.

clue.text: Slowly shift PC and get Apple, good but oddly deficient

indicators.note: lacking the odd letters, so the second and fourth letters of each word are kept

explanation.surface: Moving slowly from PC to Apple computers: good, but missing some odd things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PC' is a second definition: in British slang the plod are the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To trudge heavily and slowly is to move along laboriously.

clue.text: Looking for some cannabis, troublemaker orbits restaurant

indicators.note: some means part of, so the answer is a run of letters inside these words

explanation.surface: A troublemaker hunting for cannabis circles round a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: Double wordplay: also ORBITS rearranged, with 'troublemaker' as the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A small, informal eating place, typically French-style.

clue.text: All-nite dancing? Count on it

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so these are rearranged

parts.note: to rely on someone is to count on them

explanation.surface: An invitation to dance all night, with a promise you can depend on.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverbial sense: 'all' as in 'all alone' means wholly, completely.

clue.text: Became aware of Beryl unclothed at the metal works

parts.note: smelt, the past tense of smell, can mean sensed or became aware of

indicators.note: unclothed means stripped of its outer covering, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone spotted Beryl naked at the foundry.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant where ore is heated and melted to extract metal.

clue.text: Women's trouble

parts.note: two words for women, ma and lady, put together make a word for trouble

explanation.surface: A euphemism for a ladies' complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: MA and LADY are both women.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an ailment or illness is trouble of the bodily kind.
